items.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? Scope Conditions for Hindsight Self-Distillation in Financial Reasoning
items.abstract: Financial institutions operating under data-residency constraints are restricted to open-weight models small enough to locally host, which trail frontier systems on multi-step quantitative reasoning. On-policy distillation narrows such gaps by supervising a student on its own rollouts, but traditional OPD requires a strong external teacher, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) conditions on a full reference solution. items.title_ar: ما مدى أهمية التلميح؟ شروط النطاق للتقطير الذاتي بأثر رجعي في الاستدلال المالي
items.summary_ar: تقتصر المؤسسات المالية الخاضعة لقيود توطين البيانات على النماذج مفتوحة الأوزان الصغيرة بما يكفي للاستضافة محليًا، والتي تتخلف عن الأنظمة الرائدة في الاستدلال الكمي متعدد الخطوات. يُضيّق التقطير المباشر للسياسة هذه الفجوات عبر الإشراف على النموذج الطالب من خلال نتائجه الذاتية، لكن الطرق التقليدية

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
items.abstract: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations. Notably, in comprehensive embedding benchmarks across all modalities, EmbeddingGemma 2 establishes a new Pareto frontier, outperforming both specialist models and models two to twelve times larger. items.title: T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation
items.abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) platforms typically return several images per prompt so users can explore different visual interpretations and choose one that matches their intent. However, T2I models are usually optimized for single-image quality which comes at a cost of multi-image diversity, limiting this exploration. Diversity is also contextual: one user wants variations in background, while another wants them in artistic style, and the same user may later want variations in clothing. items.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. We propose Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), combining Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale. items.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
items.abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? items.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
items.abstract: How much of zero-shot benchmark accuracy is captured by word-level alignment between a pre-training corpus and the benchmark target? We study this question through word-level unigram cross-entropy (UCE), a tokenizer-agnostic, model-free measure of lexical alignment between a reference corpus and a target benchmark.
